proposed_statement_changes.reason: The selector coordinates and repeated universal coordinates guard nonconstant numbers of edge copies, so the frozen constant guard-list restriction is not established. In addition, explicitly listing every induced equality-or-complement pair makes the canonical encoding as large as \(O(L^2\log^2(L+2))\), rather than \(O(L\log L)\). Finally, cost-preserving rounding is proved for robust cuts; an arbitrary nonrobust auxiliary cut can separate one completion at a clause junction without its rounded occurrence endpoint doing so. The reduction remains polynomial and all graph-degree and robust-cut claims survive.

The supplied compiler proves hardness with binary signed switch coordinates and equality/complement reuse, but its global selector and universal coordinates have unbounded guard fanout. Removing only the unsupported constant-size switch clause preserves the causal and \(\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}\)-completeness conclusions.

If the budget is below the minimum separator size, \(\mathcal J_B(\mathfrak G)\) is empty and minimization over that set is undefined. The proposed statement supplies the exact feasibility equivalence and restricts the minimum-member assertion to the nonempty case.
